sentences.text: Kosmoceratops was a medium-sized ceratopsid dinosaur with an estimated length of 4.5 meters and a weight of 1.2 metric tons.
Its horns pointed upwards and to the sides before curving downwards to end in sharp tips.

The holotype skull, which is the specimen the species is based on, is nearly complete but missing the predentary bone and parts of the left face and neck frill, with a snout bent to the right from postmortem distortion.
It possessed long rows of main teeth forming complex cutting batteries containing hundreds of teeth behind a toothless beak.
Kosmoceratops possessed the most complex neck frill margin among ceratopsians, having the highest values of fractal dimensions.
Research suggests the increasing complexity of ceratopsian ornaments may be a byproduct of Cope's Rule, which links body size increase with evolutionary time.
Fossils of Kosmoceratops were discovered in Utah within the Kaiparowits Formation during the years 2006 and 2007.
The genus Kosmoceratops was described by Sampson et al. in 2010, with the name given by paleontologist Scott D. Sampson and colleagues.
Sampson and colleagues viewed the discovery as strong support for the idea of dinosaur provinces.
The teeth of ceratopsids, including Kosmoceratops, were adapted for processing fibrous plants.
Fossilized dung from the Kaiparowits Formation, potentially from Kosmoceratops, contained fragments of angiosperm wood, indicating a diet of woody browse.
Coprolites attributed to Kosmoceratops contained traces of mollusc shells, arthropod cuticle, and lizard bone, suggesting these items were ingested along with plant material.
Histological study of Kosmoceratops bones revealed a dense network of blood vessels and high osteocyte counts, indicating sustained rapid growth.
Bone microstructure evidence suggests Kosmoceratops had an elevated metabolism and was endothermic, similar to modern birds and mammals.
The absence of annual growth lines in Kosmoceratops bones suggests it could sustain growth year-round, possibly due to a more equitable southern climate compared to northern relatives.
The wetlands where Kosmoceratops lived were dominated by cypress trees up to 30 meters tall and various aquatic plants.
Better-drained areas in Kosmoceratops' habitat featured forests of 10-20 meter dicot trees and palms with fern understories.
Drier areas of the habitat were dominated by conifers up to 30 meters tall with cycads and small bushes in the understory.
Evidence suggests a pond environment for the deposition of the broken bones of the subadult or adult specimen UMNH VP 21339.
Kosmoceratops is classified as a chasmosaurine ceratopsid.
In 2010, researchers placed Kosmoceratops in the subfamily Chasmosaurinae based on skull features including a narial strut, a triangular process, and an elongated squamosal bone.
Subsequent studies in 2011 and 2013 supported the grouping of Kosmoceratops and Vagaceratops together, though other researchers have argued for different relationships.
The Kaiparowits Formation dates to the late Campanian age and was deposited on Laramidia, an island continent formed when North America was divided by the Western Interior Seaway.
Kosmoceratops lived in Utah between 76.4 and 75.5 million years ago during the late Campanian age of the Late Cretaceous.
The boundary between northern and southern dinosaur provinces on Laramidia lay around modern northern Utah and Colorado.
Kosmoceratops lived during the Upper Cretaceous period.
The functions of ceratopsian frills and horns are debated, with proposed roles including display, combat, and species recognition.
James A. Campbell and colleagues rejected the assignment of specimen CMN 8801 to Kosmoceratops in 2016, arguing the features were likely due to taphonomy or variation within Chasmosaurus.
